args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18 across us-east, us-west, and eu-west). I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all production regions. v2.3.1-rc was healthy only in staging and was not used. After rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, healthy=true, and error rate is 0.002. Next steps: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before any redeploy. Re-deploying v2.3.1 requires change-manager approval because it has never been healthy in production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1 was the unhealthy release. v2.3.1-rc was healthy only in staging, so I did not use it.
- **Result:** All regions now run v2.3.0. The service reports healthy, and the error rate dropped from 0.18 to 0.002.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback, and the verified state. It also notes that re-deploying v2.3.1 requires change-manager approval, because v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production.

The v2.3.1 failure still needs investigating before anyone redeploys it.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1 is the unhealthy release now running in all three regions. v2.3.1-rc was healthy only in staging, so it doesn't qualify. Rolling back to v2.3.0.
